# Student Handout: Seerah, History & Living Faith Today
## Level: 10 Years Old

---

## Welcome to Your Journey!
Dear student, welcome! This handout is designed for you. In these pages, we will explore some of the most exciting and important parts of our history. We will travel back in time to the final years of the Prophet Muhammad’s ﷺ life, meet the four amazing leaders who took care of the Muslim community after him, discover a famous scholar named Imam Malik who lived in the city of Madinah, and find out how his teachings traveled across the desert into Africa. Finally, we will talk about how you can be a strong, confident Muslim right now in the modern world, balancing your school, your family, and your prayers.

Let’s begin this journey of knowledge!

---

## Chapter 1: The Sunset of Prophethood and the Eternal Legacy

### 1.1 The Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*)
Imagine being forced to leave your home town, being treated badly for years, and then returning to that same city years later as a strong victor. How would you treat the people who hurt you?

In the 8th year of the Hijrah (the Migration), the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ returned to the city of Makkah. He did not enter like a proud king. Instead, he rode his camel with his head bowed so low in humility (*Tawāḍu‘*) that his chin almost touched the saddle. He was thanking Allah for His help.

When he stood before the chiefs of Quraysh—the very people who had fought against him, boycotted his family, and tried to harm the Muslims—they were terrified. They thought he would punish them. But the Prophet ﷺ looked at them and asked: *"What do you think I am going to do to you?"* They answered: *"You are a noble brother and the son of a noble brother."*

The Prophet ﷺ smiled and said: *"Go, for you are free."* 

This is known as the Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*). It teaches us that Islam values mercy (*Raḥmah*) and forgiveness over revenge.

---
> ### Vocabulary Box:
> * **Tawāḍu‘** (تَوَاضُع): Humility. Showing humbleness before Allah and not acting better than other people.
> * **Raḥmah** (رَحْمَة): Mercy. Having a soft heart and showing kindness to others.
---

### 1.2 The Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Widā‘*)
Two years later, in the 10th year of the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ performed his last pilgrimage to Makkah. It is called the Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Widā‘*). Over 100,000 Muslims joined him. 

Standing on the plains of Mount ‘Arafāt, the Prophet ﷺ gave a beautiful and famous speech. He told us:
* Our lives, our money, and our honor are sacred. We must never hurt each other.
* We must treat women with kindness and respect.
* All human beings are equal. He said: *"An Arab is not better than a non-Arab, and a non-Arab is not better than an Arab. A white person is not better than a black person, and a black person is not better than a white person—except by God-consciousness (*Taqwā*)."*

During this journey, Allah sent down the final major verse of the Quran: 
> *"Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion."* (Surah al-Mā’idah, 5:3)

---

### 1.3 The Passing of the Prophet ﷺ and His Legacy
In the 11th year of the Hijrah, on the 12th day of Rabī‘ al-Awwal, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away. It was the saddest day in the history of Madinah. The Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*) were heartbroken. Some could not believe he was gone. 

His closest friend, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, stood up and reminded everyone of a very important lesson. He read this verse from the Quran: 
> *"Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels?"* (Surah Al ‘Imran, 3:144)

Abu Bakr reminded the people: *"Whoever worshipped Muhammad, know that Muhammad has passed away. But whoever worships Allah, know that Allah is Ever-Living and never dies."*

---
> **[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School]**
> As Sunni Muslims, we believe that the Prophet ﷺ completed his work perfectly. Even though his earthly life ended, his teachings and guidance are preserved forever. In our creed, we believe the Prophets are given a special, noble spiritual life in their graves, but their work of bringing new rules is finished because the Quran is complete.
---

The Prophet ﷺ left behind no money, gold, or kingdoms. Instead, he left behind the greatest inheritance: **Knowledge (*‘Ilm*)**. The Prophet ﷺ said: *"The scholars are the heirs of the Prophets."* 

His legacy consists of:
1. **The Holy Quran:** The direct word of Allah.
2. **The Sunnah:** The living example of how the Prophet ﷺ acted, spoke, and behaved.
3. **His Family (*Ahl al-Bayt*) and Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*):** Whom we must love and respect.

---

## Chapter 2: The Four Rightly Guided Caliphs (*Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*)

After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, the Muslim community needed a leader to keep them united. This leader was called a **Caliph (*Khalīfah*)**, which means "successor" or "steward." The first four leaders are called the "Rightly Guided Caliphs" (*Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*) because they followed the path of the Prophet ﷺ very closely.

```
       ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │         THE FOUR RIGHTLY GUIDED CALIPHS                │
       ├──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬───────────┤
       │   Abu Bakr   │    'Umar     │   'Uthman    │    'Ali   │
       │  al-Siddiq   │  ibn al-Khattab│ ibn 'Affan  │ ibn Abi Talib│
       │  (11-13 AH)  │  (13-23 AH)  │  (23-35 AH)  │ (35-40 AH)│
       └──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┴───────────┘
```

### 2.1 Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: The Pillar of Strength
Abu Bakr was the Prophet's ﷺ closest friend and was chosen by the Muslims to be the first Caliph. He was known for being gentle and soft-hearted, but when the community faced danger, he became as firm as a mountain.

* **What he did:** 
  * Some tribes refused to pay Zakah (the obligatory charity for the poor). Abu Bakr insisted that Zakah must be paid, because protecting the rights of the poor is a core part of Islam.
  * **Preserving the Quran:** During a battle, many Muslims who had memorized the Quran were killed. Abu Bakr realized we needed to compile the Quran into a single book so it would never be lost. He ordered the scribe Zayd ibn Thābit to gather the written pieces of the Quran and check them carefully.

---
> **[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School]**
> In the Maliki school, Zakah is not just a personal gift you give when you feel like it. It is a strict financial duty. If a person refuses to pay Zakah, they are breaking an essential rule of Islamic community life. Abu Bakr’s actions showed that Zakah is a fundamental pillar of our society.
---

### 2.2 ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab: The Fair Leader
‘Umar was the second Caliph. He was famous for his strict justice (*‘Adl*). He was so good at separating right from wrong that the Prophet ﷺ gave him the title *Al-Fārūq* (The Distinguisher).

* **What he did:**
  * He created the **Hijri Calendar** starting from the year the Prophet ﷺ migrated to Madinah.
  * He set up departments for the government, including a public treasury called the **Bayt al-Māl** to help orphans, widows, and the poor.
  * **The Story of Jerusalem:** When the city of Jerusalem opened to Muslims, ‘Umar traveled to sign the peace treaty. He shared a camel with his servant, taking turns to ride. When they entered the city, it was the servant’s turn to ride, so the Caliph ‘Umar walked on foot, holding the camel's reins! He signed the Covenant of ‘Umar, guaranteeing that Christians could practice their religion safely in their churches.

---

### 2.3 ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan: The Generous Helper
‘Uthman was the third Caliph. He was a very wealthy businessman who spent almost all his money helping Islam. He was incredibly shy and modest (*Ḥayā’*).

* **What he did:**
  * **Standardizing the Quran:** As the Muslim lands grew, people from different countries began pronouncing the Arabic words of the Quran differently. ‘Uthman ordered that a master copy of the Quran be written down in the exact dialect of Makkah. He sent copies of this book (called the *Muṣḥaf*) to all the provinces. This is the exact Quran we read today!
  * **Patience in Trouble:** When troublemakers surrounded his house and threatened him, ‘Uthman refused to let his guards fight them. He did not want to cause bloodshed in the city of the Prophet ﷺ. He was martyred while reading the Quran.

---

### 2.4 ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib: The Gate of Wisdom
‘Ali was the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ (married to the Prophet's daughter, Fatima). He was the fourth Caliph and was famous for his bravery, deep knowledge, and wise rulings.

* **What he did:**
  * He ruled during a difficult time when there was division in the community.
  * He worked hard to restore justice, fight corruption, and ensure that government officials were honest.
  * Whenever the other Caliphs had a difficult legal question, they would ask ‘Ali because of his incredible understanding of Islamic law.

---
> **[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School]**
> Sometimes you might hear about disputes or wars that happened between the Companions during this time. In our creed, we respect **all** the Companions. We believe they were all sincere and trying their best to make the right choices for the community. We do not speak badly of any Companion of the Prophet ﷺ.
---

---

## Chapter 3: Imam Malik and the Journey of Fiqh

Have you ever wondered how scholars decide what is Halal (allowed) and Haram (forbidden)? This is called **Fiqh**, which means "deep understanding" of Islamic rules. To help us understand Fiqh, we have schools of law called **Madhhabs**. One of the most famous Madhhabs is the **Maliki school**.

### 3.1 The Star of the Scholars
Imam Malik ibn Anas was born in Madinah in the year 93 AH. He lived almost his entire life in the city where the Prophet ﷺ lived and died. He was called the *Imām Dār al-Hijrah* (The Imam of the Abode of Migration).

Imam Malik had immense love for the Prophet ﷺ. 
* He would never ride a horse or camel in Madinah, saying: *"I feel ashamed before Allah to ride an animal on the soil where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is buried."*
* When someone came to ask him about a Hadith, he would take a bath (*Ghusl*), put on his best clothes, apply perfume, and sit with great respect before speaking.
* If he was not sure about a question, he would simply say: *"I do not know."* He taught his students that saying "I do not know" is a sign of true wisdom.

---

### 3.2 The *Muwaṭṭa’*: The Approved Path
Imam Malik wrote one of the first major books in Islamic history, called the **Muwaṭṭa’**. The name means "The Approved Path." 

This book contains:
* Sayings of the Prophet ﷺ (Hadith).
* Rulings of the Companions.
* The living practice of the people of Madinah (*‘Amal*).

Imam al-Shāfi‘ī said about it: *"There is no book on earth after the Book of Allah that is more correct than the book of Malik."*

---
> **[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School - The Practice of Madinah]**
> A unique rule of the Maliki school is **‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah** (The Practice of the People of Madinah). Imam Malik argued that since thousands of Companions lived and died in Madinah, the general actions of the city's scholars were like a living Sunnah. 
> 
> For example: In the Maliki school, the primary way to pray obligatory prayers is with your arms resting naturally at your sides (*Sadl*), rather than folded over your chest. This is because Imam Malik observed that the major scholars of Madinah prayed this way. While both folding and resting the arms are valid, this shows how Fiqh decisions are based on different paths of evidence.
---

```
                       ┌─────────────────────────┐
                       │   SPREAD OF MALIKI FIQH │
                       └────────────┬────────────┘
                                    │
           ┌────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
           ▼                                                 ▼
     NORTH AFRICA                                      WEST AFRICA
  (Morocco, Tunisia)                                (Mali, Nigeria)
  Spread by scholars like                         Spread by traders & scholars;
  Sahnūn & Fatima al-Fihri                        centers like Timbuktu & jurists
  (al-Qarawiyyīn University)                      like Ahmad Baba.
```

### 3.3 How Maliki Fiqh Traveled to Africa
How did Imam Malik’s teachings leave Madinah and travel thousands of miles? 

1. **The Caravans of Students:** Students traveled from Egypt, North Africa (Tunisia, Morocco), and Spain (Al-Andalus) to study with Imam Malik in Madinah. When they returned home, they taught what they had learned.
2. **Fatima al-Fihri & al-Qarawiyyīn:** In Morocco, a wealthy Muslim woman named Fatima al-Fihri used her inheritance to build a mosque and university called **al-Qarawiyyīn** in the year 859 CE. It became a global center for studying Maliki Fiqh.
3. **The Trade Routes to West Africa:** Muslim merchants traveled across the Sahara Desert to West Africa (countries like Mali, Senegal, and Nigeria). Because these merchants were honest, fair, and followed Maliki rules of business, the local kings and citizens embraced Islam.
4. **Timbuktu:** The city of Timbuktu in Mali became a legendary center of Islamic knowledge, producing thousands of hand-written books on Fiqh, math, and science. A famous Maliki scholar from there was Ahmad Baba, who wrote many books on law.

---

## Chapter 4: Being a Muslim Kid in the Modern World

Now that we have looked at our history, let's talk about **you**. How do you live as a Muslim today? You have school, sports, games, friends, and family. Sometimes, it can feel like a lot to balance.

### 4.1 Fiqh: Your Personal Compass
Think of Fiqh not as a list of "do nots," but as a guide or compass for your life. In Islam, every single action we do fits into one of five categories. This is called **Al-Aḥkām al-Khamsah**:

1. **Compulsory (*Farḍ*):** You must do it, and you get rewarded. If you skip it, you are committing a sin (e.g., the five daily prayers).
2. **Recommended (*Mandūb*):** You get rewarded if you do it, but there is no sin if you don't (e.g., using a miswak, smiling, or helping a neighbor).
3. **Permissible (*Mubāḥ*):** Neutral actions. You can do them or not. Most things in life are here (e.g., playing football, eating apples, studying science).
4. **Disliked (*Makrūh*):** It is better not to do it, but it is not a sin (e.g., wasting water while making Wudu, playing games all day).
5. **Forbidden (*Ḥarām*):** You must avoid it. Doing it is a sin (e.g., lying, stealing, cheating in exams).

*Tip:* You can turn a *Mubāḥ* (permissible) action into an act of worship by having a good intention (*Niyyah*). For example, if you eat dinner with the intention of gaining energy to pray, your dinner becomes a rewardable action!

---

### 4.2 The Balance: Dīn and Dunyā
* **Dīn** (دِين): Your religion and relationship with Allah.
* **Dunyā** (دُنْيَا): This worldly life, including your school, hobbies, and career.

As a Muslim, you do not have to choose between them! You can be a top student in your class and a practicing Muslim at the same time. 

Here is how:
* **The Prayer Pivot:** Never say, *"I will pray when I finish my homework."* Instead, plan your homework sessions around your prayers. If you pray Asr on time, take a break, do your homework, and then pray Maghrib, you will find that Allah puts **Barakah** (blessing) in your time.
* **Good Friends (*Ṣuḥbah*):** The Prophet ﷺ told us that we are like the friends we keep. If you hang out with people who are honest, kind, and pray, it will be easy for you to do the same. If your friends use bad words or skip prayers, it will eventually affect you.
* **Modesty (*Ḥayā’*):** Being proud of who you are. You don't need to fit into trends that go against Islamic values just to look "cool." True confidence comes from knowing you are trying to please Allah.

---

## Chapter 5: Reflection and Actions

### Summary of What We Learned:
1. **Mercy is Victory:** The Conquest of Makkah proved that forgiveness is stronger than anger.
2. **The Chain of Knowledge:** The Quran and Sunnah were preserved by the Caliphs and scholars, reaching us through an unbroken chain.
3. **Living Practice:** Imam Malik showed us that the daily practice of Madinah (*‘Amal*) is a key source of guidance.
4. **Active Faith:** Being a Muslim today means using Fiqh as a compass to balance your studies (*Dunyā*) and your faith (*Dīn*).

---

### Creative Reflection Activity
Imagine you have a friend at school who is not Muslim. They ask you: *"Why do you pray five times a day? Doesn't it get in the way of your play time or your schoolwork?"*

## Part 1: Multiple Choice (Questions 1–10)
*Choose the correct answer for each question.*

### 1. In what year of the Hijrah did the Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*) take place?
* A) 2nd Year
* B) 5th Year
* C) 8th Year
* D) 10th Year

### 2. How did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enter Makkah during the Conquest?
* A) Raising his sword and shouting in victory
* B) Bowing his head in deep humility (*Tawāḍu‘*) on his camel
* C) Riding a gold carriage
* D) Demanding that his enemies be punished immediately

### 3. What did the Prophet ﷺ tell the Quraysh chiefs who had spent twenty years fighting against him?
* A) *"You must leave Makkah forever."*
* B) *"Go, for you are free."*
* C) *"You must pay a heavy fine."*
* D) *"I will take my revenge today."*

### 4. Which mountain was the Prophet ﷺ standing on when he gave his Farewell Sermon?
* A) Mount Uhud
* B) Mount Safa
* C) Mount ‘Arafāt
* D) Mount Hira

### 5. Who stood up to calm the Muslims after the Prophet ﷺ passed away, saying: *"Whoever worshipped Muhammad, know that Muhammad has passed away. But whoever worships Allah, know that Allah is Ever-Living..."*?
* A) Sayyiduna ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
* B) Sayyiduna ‘Ali ibn Abī Ṭālib
* C) Sayyiduna Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq
* D) Sayyiduna ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān

### 6. What does the Arabic word *Khalīfah* (Caliph) mean?
* A) Prophet of Allah
* B) Successor or Steward
* C) King of the World
* D) Army General

### 7. Who ordered the very first collection of the Quran's verses into a single volume (*Ṣuḥuf*)?
* A) Sayyiduna Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq
* B) Sayyiduna ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
* C) Sayyiduna ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān
* D) Imam Malik

### 8. Which Caliph established the Islamic Hijri calendar starting from the year of Migration?
* A) Sayyiduna Abu Bakr
* B) Sayyiduna ‘Umar
* C) Sayyiduna ‘Uthmān
* D) Sayyiduna ‘Alī

### 9. What is the name of the famous book of Hadith and Fiqh compiled by Imam Malik?
* A) Sahih al-Bukhari
* B) Sahih Muslim
* C) The Muwaṭṭa’
* D) The Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn

### 10. In the Maliki school, how do students pray their obligatory prayers regarding their arm position?
* A) Folding them over their chest
* B) Putting their hands behind their back
* C) Letting their arms rest naturally at their sides (*Sadl*)
* D) Raising them above their head

### 11. The Prophet ﷺ showed great ____________ (humility) by bowing his head when entering Makkah in victory.

---

## Part 3: Scenario & Short Answer (Questions 16–20)
*Read the scenarios and write 2-3 sentences to answer the questions.*

### 16. The Science Project (*Niyyah*)
* **Scenario:** Yusuf is studying for his science exam. He thinks: *"This is just a school science project, it has nothing to do with my religion."*
* **Question:** How can Yusuf change his intention (*Niyyah*) to turn his school studies into a rewardable act of worship?

### 17. The Zakah Duty
* **Scenario:** A wealthy person says: *"I don't need to pay Zakah to the community. I will just give a small amount of charity directly to my friend when I feel like it."*
* **Question:** Based on the actions of Sayyiduna Abu Bakr and the Maliki school, why is Zakah a compulsory community duty rather than just a personal choice?

### 18. Sharing the Camel
* **Scenario:** When entering Jerusalem, Caliph ‘Umar walked on foot while his servant rode the camel, because it was the servant's turn on their travel schedule.
* **Question:** What does this story teach us about how Islamic leaders treat other people and view justice?

### 19. Respect for Knowledge
* **Scenario:** A student is sitting in a classroom, talking to their friends while the teacher is reading a Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ.
* **Question:** How does this student's behavior compare to how Imam Malik prepared himself to study and teach Hadith? What should the student change?

### 20. The Five Categories of Action
* **Scenario:** Layla wants to spend her entire weekend playing video games and skipping her homework.
* **Question:** Using the five categories of action (*Al-Aḥkām al-Khamsah*), what is the difference between a permissible (*Mubāḥ*) action like playing games, and a disliked (*Makrūh*) action like wasting all her time?

### Part 1: Multiple Choice
1. **C) 8th Year.** (Fatḥ Makkah took place in Ramadan, 8 AH).
2. **B) Bowing his head in deep humility (*Tawāḍu‘*) on his camel.** (He showed gratitude to Allah instead of pride).

4. **C) Mount ‘Arafāt.** (This is where the Farewell Sermon was delivered).
5. **C) Sayyiduna Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.** (He kept the community stable and firm in their faith).
6. **B) Successor or Steward.** (A Caliph manages the political and social affairs of the community, succeeding the Prophet’s ﷺ leadership).
7. **A) Sayyiduna Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.** (He ordered the first collection of the Quran onto sheets of parchment after many memorizers died in battle).
8. **B) Sayyiduna ‘Umar.** (He chose the Migration (*Hijrah*) as the starting point of the calendar).
9. **C) The Muwaṭṭa’.** (This is Imam Malik’s compilation of Hadith, sayings of the Companions, and practices of Madinah).

# Student Handout: Seerah, History & Living Faith Today
## Level: 13 Years Old (Early Teens)

---

## Introduction: Why Study History and Law?
As a young Muslim entering your teenage years, you are starting to look at the world with a more analytical mind. You are no longer just memorizing stories; you are asking *how* and *why*. 

This handout is designed to match your intellectual curiosity. We will look at three major historical shifts and one practical, real-life question:
1. **The Transition of Prophethood to Legacy:** How did the completion of the Prophet’s ﷺ mission lead to a system of preserving knowledge?
2. **The Caliphate (*Khilāfah*):** How did the early Muslim leaders build an empire while maintaining justice and spiritual focus?
3. **The Maliki School (*Madhhab*):** How did Imam Malik code the practices of Madinah, and how did this jurisprudence shape the history of North and West Africa?
4. **Living Islam Today:** How can you use Islamic theology and law as tools to build your identity and make decisions in a busy, modern world?

---

## Chapter 1: The Transition of Prophetic Legacy

### 1.1 The Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*): Mercy as a Political Tool
In the 8th year of the Migration (8 AH), the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ entered the city of Makkah with ten thousand Companions. For twenty years, the leaders of Makkah had persecuted, tortured, and boycotted the Muslims. They had forced them out of their homes and launched multiple military campaigns to destroy them.

Under normal historical standards, a victorious general entering a defeated enemy city would expect plunder, executions, and enslavement. However, the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah in a state of absolute humility (*Tawāḍu‘*), bowing his head until his beard touched his saddle. 

When he reached the Ka‘bah, he cleansed it of its 360 idols. He then addressed the Quraysh, who stood before him waiting for their fate: *"O Quraysh! What do you think I am about to do with you?"* They replied: *"Good. You are a noble brother, son of a noble brother."* The Prophet ﷺ announced: *"Go, for you are free."* 

He granted a general amnesty, forgiving even those who had killed his beloved family members (like his uncle Hamza). This event, known as the Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*), demonstrated that the goal of Islam is the reform of hearts and the establishment of peace, rather than physical domination.

---

### 1.2 The Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Widā‘*): The Human Rights Charter
In the 10th year of the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ led his only pilgrimage after the Migration, known as the Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Widā‘*). At Mount ‘Arafāt, he delivered his historic Farewell Sermon (*Khuṭbat al-Widā‘*) to an audience of over 100,000 Companions. This speech was a summary of the social and ethical teachings of Islam:

* **Sanctity of Human Rights:** *"Your blood, your property, and your honor are as sacred as this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours."*
* **Economic Justice:** The Prophet ﷺ prohibited interest and usury (*Ribā*), which allows the rich to exploit the poor.
* **Racial Equality:** *"All mankind is from Adam and Eve. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; also a white has no superiority over a black, nor does a black have any superiority over a white, except by piety (*Taqwā*) and good action."*
* **Gender Justice:** He commanded the community to treat women with kindness, noting that they are partners with mutual rights.

During this pilgrimage, the revelation reached its completion with the verse:
> *"Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion."* (Surah al-Mā’idah, 5:3)

---

### 1.3 The Passing of the Prophet ﷺ and the Concept of Succession
On the 12th of Rabī‘ al-Awwal in the 11th year of the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ passed away in Madinah. The grief of the Companions was overwhelming. Sayyiduna ‘Umar, normally a tower of strength, was so shocked that he drew his sword and declared that anyone saying the Prophet ﷺ was dead was a hypocrite.

Sayyiduna Abu Bakr stepped forward. He recited the Quranic verse:
> *"Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful."* (Surah Al ‘Imran, 3:144)

Abu Bakr’s calm, firm leadership reminded the community that while the Prophet ﷺ was the channel of divine revelation, the object of our worship is the Ever-Living Creator. 

---
> **[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School - The Nature of Prophethood]**
> In Ash'ari creed (*‘Aqīdah*), we emphasize that the Prophet ﷺ completed his role of conveying the message perfectly. With his passing, divine revelation (*Waḥy*) ended. However, we also believe that the Prophets enjoy a special, active life in the intermediate realm (*Barzakh*) where they pray, but their earthly duties of establishing new laws have ceased. This maintains the balance: we love, respect, and follow the Prophet ﷺ, but we worship Allah alone (*Tawḥīd*).
---

The Prophet ﷺ left no wealth. Instead, he left behind a legacy of knowledge. The scholars are described as the heirs of the Prophets (*Warathat al-Anbiyā’*). The core of this legacy is the preservation of the Quran and the Sunnah, which was carried out by the Companions and formalized by the jurists.

---

## Chapter 2: The Rightly Guided Caliphs (*Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*)

After the Prophet's ﷺ passing, the political and administrative leadership of the Ummah passed to the **Rightly Guided Caliphs (*Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*)**. The word Caliph (*Khalīfah*) means a deputy or successor. They did not receive revelation, but their job was to protect the religion and govern the state according to Islamic principles.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       THE AL-KHULAFA' AL-RASHIDUN                           │
├─────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────┤
│ Abu Bakr al-Siddiq  │ Umar ibn al-Khattab│ Uthman ibn Affan  │ Ali ibn Abi   │
│   (11–13 AH)        │    (13–23 AH)     │    (23–35 AH)     │ Talib (35–40) │
├─────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ • Stabilized state  │ • Formed state    │ • Standardized the│ • Re-established │
│ • Fought apostasy   │   ministries      │   written Quran   │   legal order │
│ • Collected Quran   │ • Created Hijri   │ • Funded mosque   │ • Dealt with  │
│   into first volume │   calendar        │   expansions      │   internal    │
│                     │ • Jerusalem pact  │                   │   conflicts   │
└─────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────┘
```

### 2.1 Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: The Preserver of Unity (11–13 AH)
Abu Bakr faced immediate threats. Several Arab tribes rebelled, claiming they would no longer pay the obligatory charity (*Zakah*), while false prophets arose to divide the community. 

* **The Fiqh of Zakah:** Abu Bakr declared that he would fight anyone who separated prayer from Zakah. 
* **The Compilation:** Realizing that many Quran memorizers (*Huffāẓ*) were dying in battle, Abu Bakr ordered Zayd ibn Thabit to collect the Quran from palm branches, stones, and the hearts of men, compiling it into a single official volume (*Ṣuḥuf*).

---
> **[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School - Zakah as a Public Duty]**
> In the Maliki school, Zakah is treated as a major social duty. It is not a voluntary charity. The ruler has the right to collect it, and if someone refuses to pay it, the community must enforce it. This ensures that wealth is redistributed to protect the poorest members of society.
---

### 2.2 ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab: The Creator of Institutions (13–23 AH)
‘Umar was an administrative genius who transformed the growing state into an organized society:
* **The Hijri Calendar:** He established the Islamic calendar, using the Migration (*Hijrah*) as the starting point, emphasizing that the Muslim identity is defined by action and community purpose.
* **State Institutions:** He set up ministries (*Dīwān*), a public treasury (*Bayt al-Māl*), and a social welfare system for the needy (both Muslim and non-Muslim).
* **The Opening of Jerusalem:** When the keys of Jerusalem were handed over, ‘Umar walked on foot while his servant rode, showing humility. He signed the Covenant of ‘Umar, ensuring the safety of Christian places of worship, a historical example of religious tolerance.

### 2.3 ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan: The Standardizer of the Quran (23–35 AH)
‘Uthman ruled a massive state stretching from North Africa to Persia.
* **The Standardized Text (*Al-Muṣḥaf al-‘Uthmānī*):** As non-Arabs entered Islam, variations in reciting the Quran began to cause disputes. ‘Uthman gathered the original pages compiled under Abu Bakr, standardizing the text in the dialect of the Quraysh. He sent certified copies to the provinces and ordered all other variations to be destroyed, preserving the Quran from changes.
* **Martyrdom:** Faced with a violent rebellion by political factions, ‘Uthman refused to use military force in Madinah to protect himself, wanting to avoid shedding Muslim blood. He was assassinated while reading the Quran in his home.

### 2.4 ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib: Navigating Internal Strife (35–40 AH)
‘Ali's rule was marked by political instability and civil conflicts (*Fitnah*). Despite these pressures, he refused to compromise on justice:
* **Government Reform:** He replaced corrupt governors and insisted on complete transparency in the public treasury.
* **Judicial Wisdom:** He was the supreme judge of the Ummah, establishing rules for handling rebel groups and civil conflicts that are still studied in Islamic international law today.

---
> **[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School - Respect for the Companions]**
> In Ash'ari creed, we hold that the conflicts between the Companions (such as the Battle of Camel and Siffin) were based on differences in legal reasoning (*Ijtihād*). We believe that both sides were seeking what they thought was best for the community. We hold our tongues from criticizing them, respecting their status as the generation chosen by Allah to accompany His Prophet ﷺ.
---

---

## Chapter 3: Imam Malik, *Amal*, and the Maliki School

To understand how Islamic law is applied, we must study the **Madhhabs** (schools of jurisprudence). A Madhhab is not a sect; it is a system of legal reasoning. One of the four major Sunni schools is the **Maliki Madhhab**, founded by Imam Malik ibn Anas (93–179 AH) in Madinah.

```
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │             SOURCES OF LAW IN THE MALIKI MADHHAB        │
   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │ 1. The Holy Quran                                       │
   │ 2. The Sunnah (Hadith)                                  │
   │ 3. 'Amal Ahl al-Madīnah (Practice of the People of      │
   │    Madinah)                                             │
   │ 4. Consensus (Ijmā')                                    │
   │ 5. Analogy (Qiyās)                                      │
   │ 6. Public Interest (Maṣlaḥah Mursalah)                  │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 3.1 Who Was Imam Malik?
Imam Malik spent his entire life in Madinah, studying under the children and grandchildren of the Companions. He was known as *Imām Dār al-Hijrah* (The Imam of Madinah). 
* He had extreme respect for the Prophet's ﷺ legacy, refusing to ride an animal in Madinah out of respect for the ground where the Prophet ﷺ lay.
* He compiled the **Muwaṭṭa’** (The Approved Path), which was the first major work combining Hadith and Fiqh. 
* He was highly cautious in giving legal verdicts. He famously remarked: *"The shield of the scholar is to say 'I do not know.' If he neglects it, he will be struck down."*

### 3.2 The Unique Source: *‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah*
All Sunni schools use the Quran, Sunnah, consensus (*Ijmā‘*), and analogy (*Qiyās*). However, the Maliki school has a unique source of law: **‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah** (The Practice of the People of Madinah).

Imam Malik argued that the daily, public practices of the people of Madinah were more reliable than solitary reports of Hadith (*Khabar al-Wāḥid*). 
* **The Logic:** If ten thousand people in Madinah did an action (like measuring grain or praying in a certain way) because they saw their parents do it, who saw the Companions do it, who saw the Prophet ﷺ do it, this continuous living practice is more reliable than a single report passed down by one individual.

---
> **[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School - The Posture of Prayer (*Sadl*)]**
> A well-known example of *‘Amal* is the practice of **Sadl** (praying with the arms resting naturally at the sides). While other schools use **Qabḍ** (crossing the hands on the chest or stomach) based on individual Hadiths, the Maliki school holds that *Sadl* is preferred in obligatory prayers (*Farā’iḍ*). 
> 
> In the *Mudawwanah* (the primary collection of Maliki rulings), it is recorded that Imam Malik said he did not know of the major scholars of Madinah crossing their hands in obligatory prayers. This shows that the Maliki school prioritizes the continuous, living practice of the community over isolated written reports.
---

### 3.3 The Travel of Fiqh: From Madinah to Africa
Maliki Fiqh did not stay in Madinah. It spread to become the dominant school in Egypt, North Africa, Al-Andalus (Muslim Spain), and West Africa.

1. **The Moroccan Legacy & al-Qarawiyyīn:** Fatima al-Fihri, a wealthy Muslim woman, founded the **University of al-Qarawiyyīn** in Fez, Morocco, in 859 CE. It became the world's first university and a major hub for Maliki scholarship.
2. **The Saharan Trade Routes:** Islam spread to West Africa through peaceful trade. Muslim merchants from North Africa traveled across the Sahara. Their honesty, fair pricing, and clear contracts—all guided by Maliki commercial law—inspired local empires like Mali and Songhai to embrace Islam.
3. **Timbuktu and Ahmad Baba:** The city of Timbuktu in modern-day Mali became a global center of learning. Ahmad Baba al-Timbukti (d. 1627 CE) was a world-renowned Maliki jurist whose legal verdicts were respected across North Africa.
4. **The Sokoto Caliphate:** In the 18th century, Sheikh Usman dan Fodio led a major educational reform in West Africa, establishing a society run under Maliki law, focusing on women's education and public justice.

---

## Chapter 4: Living Faith in a Secular Age

As a young Muslim today, you live in a world that is highly connected, fast-paced, and often secular (meaning it separates daily life from God). Balancing your faith, studies, and social life requires understanding how Islam applies to your daily decisions.

### 4.1 The Five Rulings (*Al-Aḥkām al-Khamsah*) as your Compass
Instead of viewing Islamic law as a set of rules designed to restrict you, look at it as a compass. Every action you perform falls into one of five categories:

```
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │          AL-AHKAM AL-KHAMSAH           │
                  ├───────────┬────────────────────────────┤
                  │   Farḍ    │ Compulsory (e.g., Prayer)  │
                  │  Mandūb   │ Recommended (e.g., Sadaqah)│
                  │  Mubāḥ    │ Permissible (e.g., Hobbies)│
                  │  Makrūh   │ Disliked (e.g., Gossip)    │
                  │  Ḥarām    │ Forbidden (e.g., Stealing) │
                  └───────────┴────────────────────────────┘
```

* **Intention (*Niyyah*):** You can elevate a neutral (*Mubāḥ*) action into a rewardable act of worship by changing your intention. For example, playing video games to relax your mind after a long day of study is *Mubāḥ*. But studying science to help cure diseases for the sake of Allah turns your daily schoolwork into a form of worship (*‘Ibādah*).

---
> **[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School - Human Agency and Allah's Will]**
> In Ash'ari theology, we believe that Allah is the Creator of all causes and effects. However, Allah has given human beings choice and the ability to "acquire" (*Kasb*) their actions. This means you are responsible for the choices you make. We do not say: *"It was written that I fail, so I won't study."* Instead, we work hard and put our trust in Allah (*Tawakkul*), knowing that our effort is our responsibility, and the outcome is created by Allah.
---

### 4.2 Practical Strategy: Balancing Studies and Prayer
One of the most common challenges for teenagers is time management.
* **The Pivot Point:** Do not try to fit your prayers into your busy study and social schedule. Instead, build your schedule around your prayers. 
* **The Benefit:** Structuring your day around the five prayers creates natural breaks for your mind, increases focus, and brings blessing (*Barakah*) into your time.
* **Company (*Ṣuḥbah*):** The Prophet ﷺ said: *"A person is upon the religion of his close friend, so let one of you look to whom he takes as a friend."* Peer pressure is real. Surrounding yourself with friends who value prayer and honesty makes it easier for you to stay strong in your identity.

* C) The destruction of non-Muslim houses of worship

* C) To add new chapters to the Quran

* D) The trade contracts signed in the marketplace of Madinah

17. **Explanation:** The logic is that a solitary Hadith (*Khabar al-Wāḥid*) is passed down through a single chain of narrators and is subject to error or misunderstanding. It is highly unlikely that an entire city would collectively fabricate or alter a daily, public action like prayer posture or market weights.

### 11. The scholars who preserve, practice, and pass on the teachings of the Quran and Sunnah are called ____________ (the heirs of the Prophets).
### 12. The Ash'ari creedal concept of ____________ (acquisition) states that while Allah creates all actions, humans choose and acquire them, making them responsible for their choices.
### 13. The ____________ is the primary text of Maliki jurisprudence that compiles the legal answers and rulings of Imam Malik, recorded by his student Ibn al-Qasim.
### 14. Caliph ‘Umar established the ____________, which served as the public treasury to manage state funds and assist the poor.
### 15. The term ____________ refers to the healthy diversity of opinion among jurists, which Imam Malik respected when he refused to force everyone to follow his book.

---

## Part 3: Scenario & Critical Reflection (Questions 16–20)
*Analyze the scenarios below and write a short essay response (3-5 sentences) for each.*

### 16. The Modern Career vs. Prayer Schedule
* **Scenario:** Kareem has a busy high school schedule. He is joining the school debate club and has basketball practice immediately after classes. He tells his mom: *"I will just combine my Dhuhr, Asr, and Maghrib prayers at night because my schedule is too packed to pray at school."*
* **Question:** How would you advise Kareem using the concept of Fiqh as a compass and the concept of *Barakah* (blessing in time) when organizing his daily schedule?

### 17. Evaluating the Logic of *‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah*
* **Scenario:** A student asks: *"Why did Imam Malik prefer the practice of the people of Madinah over a solitary Hadith report? Isn't a written Hadith always more reliable than what a crowd of people are doing?"*
* **Question:** Explain the legal logic of *‘Amal*. Why is the collective, continuous action of a city like Madinah considered a strong, living transmission of the Sunnah?

### 18. Standardization and Unity
* **Scenario:** Imagine if Caliph ‘Uthmān had not standardized the written text of the Quran and had allowed every region to write the Quran in their local dialects and pronunciations.
* **Question:** What could have been the consequences for the unity of the global Muslim community and the preservation of the Quranic text?

### 19. Media Consumption and the Five Rulings
* **Scenario:** Yasmin spends two hours every day watching random videos on social media. She argues: *"Watching videos is not Haram, so I am not doing anything wrong."*
* **Question:** Help Yasmin analyze her activity using the five categories of action (*Al-Aḥkām al-Khamsah*). How can she use her intention (*Niyyah*) to change how she uses her screen time?

### 20. Theology in Action: Preparing for Exams
* **Scenario:** A teen student says: *"Everything is written by Allah. If Allah has decreed that I will fail my exam, studying won't change anything. If He has decreed I will pass, I will pass anyway without studying. So I will just play games."*
* **Question:** Correct this student's understanding using the Ash'ari creedal concepts of human agency (*Kasb*), cause and effect, and relying on Allah (*Tawakkul*).

# Teacher Presentation: Seerah, History & Living Faith Today

Welcome to the presentation slide deck for teachers. Each slide includes the slide title, slide text (bullet points to be displayed to students), and detailed **Teacher Notes** for explanation and classroom discussion.

---

## Slide 1: Title Slide
### Seerah, History & Living Faith Today

* **Module 1:** The Later Years and Legacy of the Prophet ﷺ
* **Module 2:** The Rightly Guided Caliphs (*Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*)
* **Module 3:** Imam Malik, the *Muwaṭṭa’*, and the Spread of Maliki Fiqh
* **Module 4:** Being a Muslim in the Modern World
* **Theme:** Building Fiqh Literacy & Faith-Identity Balance

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Assalāmu ‘alaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh. Welcome, respected teacher. This curriculum is designed to guide students through the transition from Prophetic history to the formalization of Islamic law (*Fiqh*), and finally to their own practical lives as modern Muslims. 

This slide deck serves as a visual aid. The core of the learning will come from your narrative delivery, guided by these notes. We will focus specifically on the Maliki school of jurisprudence (*Madhhab*) and the Ash'ari school of theology (*‘Aqīdah*). We aim to build a strong sense of intellectual heritage, illustrating how the practices of the Prophet ﷺ were preserved in Madinah, coded by Imam Malik, carried into Africa, and are lived by us today.

---

## Slide 2: Course Map & Objective
### Linking History to Living Practice

* **The Prophetic Legacy:** Understanding how the Prophet ﷺ completed his message.
* **The Golden Chain:** How the Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*) passed this light to the next generations.
* **The Madinah Connection:** Why Madinah is the cradle of Maliki Fiqh.
* **Living the Legacy:** Applying these timeless principles to your daily life.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
In this course, we are not just looking at dates and events as dead history. Instead, we are tracing a golden line of transmission. Students should realize that the way we pray, make decisions, and view our creator today is directly connected to the actions of the Prophet ﷺ, preserved by the scholars of Madinah, and structured into a system of jurisprudence. 

Make sure to emphasize that history is the soil from which our identity grows. By understanding how Islam was preserved and how it traveled to different parts of the world—especially North and West Africa—students will see Islam as a global, deeply rooted faith that is fully capable of addressing modern challenges.

---

## Slide 3: The Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*)
### The Triumph of Mercy

* **Year of occurrence:** 8th Year of Hijrah.
* **The Entry:** The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah on his camel, bowing his head in humility (*Tawāḍu‘*), not as a proud conqueror.
* **General Amnesty:** He ﷺ forgave his former enemies who had persecuted Muslims for twenty years.
* **The Saying:** *"Go, for you are free."*
* **Cleansing the Ka‘bah:** Removal of idols while maintaining the sacredness of the Sanctuary.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
We begin the historical narrative in the later years of the Prophet’s ﷺ life. The Conquest of Makkah (*Fatḥ Makkah*) is one of the greatest examples of political and spiritual victory in human history. Explain to the students that instead of seeking revenge against the Quraysh, who had tortured the early Muslims, boycotted them, and fought battles against them, the Prophet ﷺ showed unmatched mercy (*Raḥmah*). 

He quoted Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) saying, *"No blame is upon you today."* Point out the character of the Prophet ﷺ—he did not enter Makkah with trumpet blasts and a raised sword; rather, his chin touched the saddle of his camel out of humility and gratitude to Allah. This victory shows that the goal of Islam is the guidance of hearts, not the destruction of people.

---

## Slide 4: The Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Widā‘*)
### The Completion of the Message

* **Year:** 10th Year of Hijrah.
* **The Gathering:** Over 100,000 Companions gathered in the plains of ‘Arafāt.
* **The Final Sermon:**
  * Sanctity of life, property, and honor.
  * Prohibition of interest/usury (*Ribā*).
  * Equal status of all races: *"No Arab is superior to a non-Arab..."*
  * Good treatment of women.
* **The Verse of Completion:** Surah al-Mā’idah (5:3) was revealed.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
The Farewell Pilgrimage (*Ḥajjat al-Widā‘*) represents the peak of the Prophetic mission. The Prophet ﷺ delivered a historic speech at Mount ‘Arafāt. Highlight the key points of the sermon: the equality of human beings based on God-consciousness (*Taqwā*), the protection of human rights, and the elimination of pre-Islamic injustices such as tribalism and usury (*Ribā*). 

During this pilgrimage, Allah revealed the verse: *"Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion."* Explain to the students that this verse marked the completion of the revelation of rules, indicating that the Prophet's ﷺ time on Earth was drawing to a close.

---

## Slide 5: The Passing of the Messenger ﷺ
### The Loss of the Prophet and the Transition

* **Date:** 12th of Rabī‘ al-Awwal, 11th Year of Hijrah.
* **The Crisis:** The intense grief of the Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*).
* **Abu Bakr's Leadership:** Reassuring the community using Quranic verses.
* **The Eternal Truth:** Surah Al ‘Imran (3:144): *"Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him."*
* **Preserving the Mission:** The physical presence of the Prophet ﷺ ended, but his guidance remains eternal.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School]
In Ash'ari creed, we affirm that the Prophets of Allah are alive in their graves in a state of the *Barzakh* (the intermediate realm), praying and experiencing a spiritual life that suits their noble status, which is different from normal deceased people. However, their earthly life has ended, and their legal and physical leadership transitioned to the community.

Discuss the emotional weight of this event. The Companions were devastated; Sayyiduna ‘Umar could not believe it. Sayyiduna Abu Bakr showed immense stability. He stepped forward and delivered the famous statement: *"Whoever worshipped Muhammad, know that Muhammad has passed away. But whoever worships Allah, know that Allah is Ever-Living and never dies."* This lesson highlights that our worship is for Allah alone, and the Prophet ﷺ successfully delivered the message.

---

## Slide 6: The Prophetic Legacy
### Inheritance of Knowledge (*Warathat al-Anbiyā’*)

* **Prophets leave no wealth:** They do not leave behind gold or silver coins (*Dīnār* or *Dirham*).
* **The Real Inheritance:** Divine Knowledge (*‘Ilm*).
* **Who are the heirs?** The scholars (*‘Ulamā’*) who preserve and practice this knowledge.
* **The Core Legacy:**
  1. The Holy Quran (The Word of Allah).
  2. The Sunnah (The Prophetic Model).
  3. The Love of his Family (*Ahl al-Bayt*) and respect for his Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*).

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Explain the Hadith: *"The scholars are the heirs of the Prophets."* Make the students realize that knowledge is a sacred trust. When the Prophet ﷺ left this world, he did not leave a physical kingdom for his family to inherit. Rather, he left the ultimate gift: sacred knowledge. 

Highlight that this legacy must be handled with care. The preservation of the Sunnah was not a random project; it was a meticulous, scientific effort carried out by the Companions and the generations that followed them. Underline that loving the Prophet's family (*Ahl al-Bayt*) and respecting all his Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*) are key markers of the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah.

---

## Slide 7: What is the Caliphate? (*Khilāfah*)
### The Rightly Guided Caliphs (*Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*)

* **Definition:** *Khilāfah* means succession or stewardship of the community.
* **The Period:** The first four leaders after the Prophet ﷺ.
* **The Title:** "Rightly Guided" (*Rāshidūn*) because they followed the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ closely in leadership.
* **Main Achievements:**
  * Maintaining unity during crises.
  * Preservation and compilation of the Quran.
  * Administration of justice and establishing public services.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Define the word *Khilāfah* literally as "succession." The Caliph (*Khalīfah*) does not receive divine revelation—revelation ended with the Prophet ﷺ. Rather, the Caliph's job is to protect the religion and manage the worldly affairs of the community according to Islamic values. 

Introduce the term *Al-Khulafā’ al-Rāshidūn*. Explain that the Prophet ﷺ praised this era, stating that we should hold fast to their path. They faced unique, unprecedented issues and solved them using mutual consultation (*Shūrā*), showing us how to apply Islamic principles as the world changes.

---

## Slide 8: Caliph 1: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (11–13 AH)
### The Pillar of Stability

* **Title:** *Al-Ṣiddīq* (The Truthful / The Affirmer of Truth).
* **Major Crises Handled:**
  * Grief over the Prophet's passing.
  * The Wars of Apostasy (*Riddah*): Groups refusing to pay Zakah or claiming fake prophethood.
* **Quran Preservation:** He ordered the first collection of the Quran into a single volume (*Ṣuḥuf*) under the guidance of Zayd ibn Thābit.
* **Character:** Soft-hearted yet incredibly firm in defending the faith.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Sayyiduna Abu Bakr was the closest friend of the Prophet ﷺ. When the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abu Bakr stood as the pillar of the community. Some Arab tribes thought that Zakah was only due to the Prophet ﷺ and refused to pay it to Abu Bakr. Others followed false prophets like Musaylimah. 

[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School]
In the Maliki school, we learn that Zakah is a compulsory social duty, not just a private charity. Abu Bakr’s stance proves that the state must ensure the financial rights of the poor are protected. Explain how he initiated the collection of the Quran after many Quran memorizers (*Huffāẓ*) were martyred in the battle of Yamamah, safeguarding the text for all future generations.

---

## Slide 9: Caliph 2: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (13–23 AH)
### The Architect of Justice

* **Title:** *Al-Fārūq* (The Distinguisher between Right and Wrong).
* **Administrative Genius:**
  * Established the Islamic Hijri calendar starting from the Migration (*Hijrah*).
  * Created ministries, departments (*Dīwān*), a postal system, and public treasuries (*Bayt al-Māl*).
* **Justice:** Known for his strict adherence to justice, refusing any favoritism.
* **Expansion:** Jerusalem opened peacefully under his rule, granting safety to the Christian population through the Covenant of ‘Umar.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Sayyiduna ‘Umar was a visionary leader. He took the growing Muslim community and organized it into a fully functioning state. He established the Hijri calendar, choosing the Migration (*Hijrah*) as the starting point rather than the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, highlighting that Islam is defined by action and community movement. 

Focus on his opening of Jerusalem. He entered the city walking beside his servant, who was riding the camel because it was the servant’s turn on their travel schedule. He signed a peace treaty ensuring that Christian churches and lives were protected. This demonstrates that Islamic law values religious freedom and human dignity.

---

## Slide 10: Caliph 3: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (23–35 AH)
### The Promoter of Unity

* **Title:** *Dhū al-Nūrayn* (Possessor of the Two Lights, having married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ).
* **Major Achievement:** The Compilation of the Quran (*Al-Muṣḥaf al-‘Uthmānī*).
  * Standardized the pronunciation and script to prevent disputes.
  * Sent certified copies to all major Muslim provinces.
* **Generosity:** Funded the expansion of the Prophet's Mosque and bought the Well of Rūmah for public use.
* **Patience:** Faced rebellion with dignity, refusing to shed Muslim blood to defend himself.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Sayyiduna ‘Uthman was famous for his modesty (*Ḥayā’*) and immense generosity. The biggest challenge during his rule was that as non-Arabs entered Islam, they began reciting the Quran with different regional accents, leading to arguments about which recitation was correct. 

‘Uthman acted decisively. He collected the original pages compiled by Abu Bakr and ordered copies to be written in the dialect of the Quraysh. This standard edition is called the *Muṣḥaf*. Emphasize his ultimate sacrifice: when rebels surrounded his house, he refused to let the Companions fight them, wanting to avoid bloodshed in the city of the Prophet ﷺ. He was martyred while reading the Quran.

---

## Slide 11: Caliph 4: ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (35–40 AH)
### The Gate of Knowledge

* **Relationship:** Cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ (married to Sayyidah Fāṭimah).
* **Key Attributes:** Famous for his bravery, wisdom, and deep knowledge of jurisprudence.
* **Rule:** A period of internal trial and tribulation (*Fitnah*).
* **Major Focus:**
  * Re-establishing law and order.
  * Fighting corruption and insisting on complete integrity in government.
* **Legacy:** His rulings in judicial matters serve as major foundations for Islamic law.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School]
In Sunni theology (Ash'ari creed), we respect all the Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*). We hold that the conflicts between them (such as the battles of Jamal and Siffin) were based on differences in legal reasoning (*Ijtihād*). We do not curse or speak ill of any of them. Sayyiduna ‘Ali was correct in his political position, and those who opposed him were mistaken in their analysis, but all of them acted out of a desire to do what they thought was best for the Ummah.

Explain to students that Sayyiduna ‘Ali faced the most difficult political climate, yet he maintained high ethical standards. He did not compromise on justice. His deep understanding of the Quran and Sunnah was so respected that the previous Caliphs constantly consulted him on complex legal cases.

---

## Slide 12: The Golden Chain of Madinah
### How Knowledge Was Preserved

* **The Core Idea:** The practice of Islam was passed down visually, not just through texts.
* **The Madinan Legacy:** Madinah was where the Prophet ﷺ lived and died, and where the Quran was put into practice daily.
* **The Transmission Path:**
  1. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
  2. The Companions in Madinah (e.g., Ibn Umar, Aisha, Zayd ibn Thabit).
  3. The Successors (The Seven Fuqaha of Madinah).
  4. Imam Malik ibn Anas.
  5. The Students of Imam Malik (carrying it to North and West Africa).

---
#### Teacher Notes:
How do we know how the Prophet ﷺ prayed, fasted, and lived? It was through this unbroken chain of transmission. This slide introduces the concept of *‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah* (The Practice of the People of Madinah). 

Explain that when the Prophet ﷺ passed away, thousands of Companions remained in Madinah. They taught their children, who taught their children. This created a living, breathing model of Islam. Imam Malik was born in this environment. He argued that if thousands of people in Madinah did an action generation-after-generation, it was more reliable than a single person reporting a Hadith that contradicted it. This is a unique feature of the Maliki school.

---

## Slide 13: Imam Malik: The Star of the Scholars
### The Scholar of Madinah (93–179 AH)

* **Name:** Mālik ibn Anas ibn Mālik al-Aṣbaḥī.
* **Birthplace:** Madinah (lived and died there, rarely leaving).
* **Title:** *Imām Dār al-Hijrah* (The Leader of the Abode of Migration).
* **Respect for Hadith:**
  * He would take a bath, put on clean clothes, apply perfume, and sit with gravity before teaching Hadith.
* **Intellectual Humility:** Famous for saying *"I do not know"* (*Lā adrī*) to questions he was not certain about.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Imam Malik is the founder of the Maliki school. He was born in the year 93 AH, meaning he was born during the time of the younger Companions and studied under the Successors (*Tābi‘ūn*). He was highly respected for his memory and intelligence. 

Tell the story of his respect for the words of the Prophet ﷺ: he never rode a horse or camel in Madinah, saying he felt ashamed to trample with animal hooves the soil where the Prophet ﷺ was buried. When asked questions, he was extremely cautious. Once, a man traveled for months to ask him forty questions, and Imam Malik answered "I do not know" to thirty-six of them. Teach the students that saying "I do not know" is a sign of true knowledge and sincerity.

---

## Slide 14: The *Muwaṭṭa’* of Imam Malik
### The First Great Book of Islam

* **Meaning of the title:** "The Approved/Smoothed Path."
* **Nature of the book:** A combined book of Hadith (sayings of the Prophet ﷺ) and Fiqh (legal rulings).
* **Content:**
  * Hadith of the Prophet ﷺ.
  * Sayings of the Companions (*Ṣaḥābah*).
  * Rulings of the Successors (*Tābi‘ūn*).
  * The Practice of Madinah (*‘Amal*).
* **Praise:** Imam al-Shāfi‘ī said: *"There is no book on earth after the Book of Allah that is more correct than the book of Malik."*

---
#### Teacher Notes:
The *Muwaṭṭa’* is a landmark in Islamic history. Before Imam al-Bukhari or Imam Muslim wrote their books of Hadith, Imam Malik compiled the *Muwaṭṭa’*. The Caliph of the time, Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, wanted to force all Muslims to follow the *Muwaṭṭa’* as the law of the land. 

[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School]
Imam Malik refused the Caliph's offer! He said: *"The Companions of the Prophet scattered to different lands, and they carry different practices. Leave the people to what they have chosen."* This shows Imam Malik's respect for diversity of opinion (*Ikhtilāf*) and his refusal to enforce a single legal code by state power.

---

## Slide 15: The Practice of Madinah (*‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah*)
### The Core of Maliki Jurisprudence

* **Concept:** The daily practice of the people of Madinah.
* **Why it matters:**
  * The Prophet ﷺ lived there for ten years.
  * Thousands of Companions practiced Islam under his supervision.
  * This practice was passed down to the next generation collectively (*Tawātur*).
* **Maliki Rule Example: *Sadl* (Praying with arms at the side).**
  * While other schools hold that crossing the hands is sunnah, the dominant Maliki opinion is to pray with arms hanging naturally, because this was the continuous practice of the scholars of Madinah.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
[Fiqh Focus: Maliki School]
Let’s explain *‘Amal Ahl al-Madīnah* using a modern analogy: if you want to know how a game is played, you don’t just read a rulebook; you watch the people who invented the game play it. The people of Madinah saw the Prophet ﷺ pray every day. 

An example of this is *Sadl* (praying with the arms resting at the sides). In the Maliki school, this is the primary and preferred method in obligatory prayers (*Farā’iḍ*), as recorded in the *Mudawwanah* (the primary text of Maliki rulings). This is because the early scholars of Madinah, including the seven great jurists, did not cross their hands in their obligatory prayers. Point out to students that both methods (*Sadl* and *Qabḍ* - crossing hands) are valid, but they reflect different ways of analyzing the evidence.

---

## Slide 16: The Spread of Maliki Fiqh to North Africa
### The Caravan of Knowledge

* **How did it travel?** Students of Imam Malik returned to their home regions.
* **Key Scholars:**
  * **Ibn al-Qāsim:** Compiled Imam Malik's rulings into the *Mudawwanah*.
  * **Sahnūn:** A Tunisian scholar who organized and spread the school across North Africa.
  * **Asad ibn al-Furāt:** A scholar and military leader who opened Sicily.
* **Centers of Learning:**
  * The University of al-Qarawiyyīn in Fez, Morocco (founded by Fatima al-Fihri).
  * Kairouan in Tunisia.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Explain how knowledge spreads. It is not through conquest, but through students who travel, study, and return to teach. Students of Imam Malik came from Egypt, North Africa (Ifriqiya), and Al-Andalus (Spain). They sat in his circle, memorized his rulings, and took them back home. 

Mention Fatima al-Fihri, a wealthy Muslim woman who founded the University of al-Qarawiyyīn in Fez, Morocco, in 859 CE. It is recognized by UNESCO as the oldest continuously operating university in the world, and it was a major center for Maliki jurisprudence. This shows the role of women in funding and building Islamic education.

---

## Slide 17: Maliki Fiqh in West Africa
### The Timbuktu Legacy

* **Trade Routes:** Islam spread to West Africa through peaceful trade and scholarly networks, not war.
* **The Empires:** Mali and Songhai Empires embraced the Maliki school.
* **Timbuktu:** A world-famous center of Islamic scholarship with millions of manuscripts.
* **Key Scholars:**
  * **Ahmad Bābā al-Timbuktī:** A great Maliki jurist who wrote over 40 books.
  * **Sheikh Usman dan Fodio:** A West African reformer who established the Sokoto Caliphate based on Maliki law.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Many students do not know that West Africa has a rich, centuries-old Islamic history. Islam did not spread to West Africa by the sword, but by Muslim traders who traveled across the Sahara Desert. These traders were known for their honesty, which was shaped by Maliki rules of business. 

Timbuktu in modern-day Mali became a global hub of learning. Scholars from all over the Muslim world came to study there. Ahmad Baba of Timbuktu was so famous for his legal verdicts (*Fatāwā*) that scholars in North Africa regularly consulted him. Emphasize that West Africa produced massive libraries of manuscripts covering astronomy, medicine, math, and jurisprudence, all within the Maliki framework.

---

## Slide 18: Being a Muslim in the Modern World
### Fiqh as a Compass, Not a Cage

* **The Challenge:** Living in a society that doesn't always value faith.
* **The Solution:** Viewing *Fiqh* (understanding of law) as a guide for daily life.
* **Every action has a ruling:**
  * **Compulsory (*Farḍ*):** Five daily prayers, fasting.
  * **Recommended (*Mandūb*):** Smiling, extra charity.
  * **Permissible (*Mubāḥ*):** Sports, studying science.
  * **Disliked (*Makrūh*):** Wasting time, playing harmful games.
  * **Prohibited (*Ḥarām*):** Lying, cheating.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Transitioning from history to the modern world, we must teach students how to live their faith. Many youth view Islamic law (*Sharī‘ah* and *Fiqh*) as a list of restrictions. We need to reframe this: Fiqh is a compass that helps you navigate life. 

Explain the five categories of human actions (*Al-Aḥkām al-Khamsah*). Show them that the vast majority of things in the world are *Mubāḥ* (permissible). Playing basketball, learning coding, and eating pizza are all permissible and can even become rewarding acts of worship if done with a good intention (*Niyyah*), such as keeping the body healthy or preparing to serve the community.

---

## Slide 19: Balancing Faith, Studies, and Identity
### The Scale of Priorities

* **Faith (*Dīn*):** Your connection to Allah.
* **Life (*Dunyā*):** Your schoolwork, physical health, and family duties.
* **Balancing the Scale:**
  * Pray on time (*Ṣalāt al-Waqt*). Plan your study sessions around your prayers.
  * Intention (*Niyyah*): Turn your school studies into worship by intending to help the Ummah.
  * Good Company (*Ṣuḥbah*): Surrounding yourself with friends who remind you of Allah.

---
#### Teacher Notes:
[Creed Focus: Ash'ari School]
In Ash'ari theology, we understand that everything in the universe happens by the will and power of Allah. However, Allah has given us choices and the ability to acquire our actions (*Kasb*). Therefore, we are responsible for how we manage our time and make decisions.

Teach the students how to schedule their day. Many students complain they don't have time to pray because of homework or sports. Tell them to change their mindset: do not fit prayer into your schedule; fit your schedule around your prayers. If you pray Dhuhr, Asr, and Maghrib on time, your time will be blessed (*Barakah*). Explain that studying biology, math, or history with the intention to benefit humanity is a form of worship.

---

## Slide 20: Faith in Action: Identity and Modesty
### Standing Strong in Your Identity

* **Modesty (*Ḥayā’*):** A core character trait of a Muslim.
* **Social Pressures:** Dealing with peer pressure, social media, and trends that contradict Islamic values.
* **The Prophet's Model:** Being kind, confident, and polite, without compromising on principles.
* **Proud but Humble:** Representing Islam through excellent character (*Akhlāq*).

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Modesty (*Ḥayā’*) is not just about clothing; it is a state of the heart that prevents a person from doing bad deeds. In the modern world, youth are bombarded with pressure to conform to un-Islamic values on social media, in school, and in entertainment. 

Teach them that a Muslim does not follow trends blindly. A Muslim is a leader, not a follower of fashion or online challenges that lack modesty or safety. Use the concept of *Akhlāq* (excellent character): the best way to defend your identity is to be the most honest, kindest, and most helpful student in your school. This is how the early merchants spread Islam in West Africa, and it is how we must live today.

---

## Slide 21: Conclusion & Reflection
### Your Legacy Starts Today

* **Review:**
  * The Prophet ﷺ completed his mission and left an inheritance of knowledge.
  * The Caliphs protected the community and compiled the Quran.
  * Imam Malik coded the living practice of Madinah.
  * Scholars carried this legacy across continents into Africa and then to us.
* **Your Part:** How will you preserve and pass on this legacy in your own life?

---
#### Teacher Notes:
Summarize the journey we have taken. We started in Makkah and Madinah, watched the message stabilize under the Rightly Guided Caliphs, saw it coded into jurisprudence by Imam Malik, watched it travel through the sands of the Sahara to West Africa, and finally brought it into our own classrooms and homes today. 

End the lesson by challenging the students: this legacy has survived for over 1,400 years and has been passed down by millions of scholars, teachers, and parents. Now, the baton is in their hands. What will they do with this inheritance of knowledge?

---

## Slide 22: Sources & References
### For Further Reading & Authentication

1. **Al-Muwaṭṭa’** of Imam Mālik ibn Anas.
2. **Al-Shifā’ bi-Ta‘rīf Ḥuqūq al-Muṣṭafā** by Qadi ‘Iyad al-Yahsubi.
3. **Tartīb al-Madārik wa-Taqrīb al-Masālik** by Qadi ‘Iyad al-Yahsubi.
4. **The History of the Khalifahs** by Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti.
5. **The Creed of Imam al-Ghazali** (*Al-Qawā‘id al-‘Aqā’id*).

# Teacher Presentation: Seerah, History & Living Faith Today

Welcome to the presentation slide deck for teachers. Each slide includes the slide title, slide text (bullet points to be displayed to students), and detailed **Teacher Notes** for explanation and classroom discussion.
